PullRequest.Title: Don't cache prompt discovery results from a cancelled scan
PullRequest.Body:
Follow-up to #338883, addressing the Copilot review comment on that PR.

### Problem

#338883 made the filesystem branches of `computeListPromptFiles` report cancellation as an error so a cancelled scan could not be cached as a permanent "no prompt files" answer.

That left one branch uncovered. `ExtensionPromptFileService._listFromProviders` bails out of its provider loop **without** throwing:

```ts
for (const providerEntry of providers) {
    if (token.isCancellationRequested) {
        break;              // returns a partial result, no throw
    }
```

So if cancellation lands while the extension-provider branch is running and the filesystem branches either already finished or are policy-blocked (`allowStandalone === false` makes them literal `[]`), the combined `Promise.all` resolves normally. The partial list is then stored in `cachedFileLocations[type]` and never evicted — the exact state #338883 set out to fix.

This is reachable in practice, not theoretical: extension activation (`activateByEvent`) is slow relative to the file scans, so the provider branch is often the last one outstanding.

### Change

Re-check the token after the combined computation, so no branch that swallows cancellation can have its result accepted and cached:

```ts
// A branch may stop early on cancellation without throwing (extension
// providers do), so re-check before this result is accepted and cached.
if (token.isCancellationRequested) {
    throw new CancellationError();
}
```

The guard is placed at the combined result rather than in `_listFromProviders`, because that loop's tolerance is intentional (it stops calling further providers without erroring), and a single choke point also covers any future branch that swallows cancellation.

### Testing

Added `does not cache a partial result when a provider swallows cancellation`. It enables the strict-plugin-only lockdown so the filesystem branches are literal `[]`, making the provider the only possible cancellation source — the test is therefore deterministic and specifically covers this gap rather than the path already fixed in #338883.

| Command | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `./scripts/test.sh --runGlob "**/contrib/chat/test/**/promptSyntax/**/*.test.js"` | passed (802 passing) |
| `./scripts/test.sh --runGlob "**/contrib/chat/test/**/*.test.js"` | 11032 passing, 2 pre-existing failures |
| `npm run typecheck-client` | passed |

The new test was verified to fail without the guard (`AssertionError: Missing expected rejection (CancellationError)`) and pass with it.

The 2 remaining failures are pre-existing and unrelated — `agentHostChatContribution.test.ts` hardcodes `/home/test-user` as the home directory and fails identically on a clean checkout of `main`.

Scenarios.Scenario: Cold prompt-file discovery for one prompt type, including cancellation during an extension provider
Scenarios.CriticalPath: listPromptFiles awaits computeListPromptFiles, which awaits all five source branches; extension discovery waits for extension registration, activation, and sequential provider callbacks, while standalone discovery waits for local/user filesystem search. The new token check runs only after all branches settle and is therefore on the critical path, but it is a constant-time read.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve or search configured local and user prompt locations and enumerate matching files.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two top-level branches per uncached prompt type (local and user), with configured locations processed sequentially inside each branch; effective calls scale with deduplicated configured source locations and workspace roots.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same local and user scans ran with the same cardinality and parallel placement before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Both branches must finish before the combined discovery result can be returned. Cancellation is already surfaced from these branches after each location.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Wait for extension registration, activate extensions for the prompt-type activation event, and invoke each registered prompt-file provider.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One activation event per uncached type discovery, then one callback per provider of that type, sequentially; in the strict-plugin-only test there is one provider and zero standalone filesystem branches.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The identical activation and provider calls ran before the diff, but a normally resolved partial provider result could pass through to cache admission.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Provider activation/callbacks are awaited by the extension branch and the combined Promise.all. A provider may observe cancellation and return normally, which is the condition handled by the added guard.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Configured prompt source locations, workspace roots, and registered providers for one prompt type. Cancellation does not add a boundary call; a later explicit request starts one fresh discovery after the canceled result is rejected.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The five source branches run under one Promise.all. Local and user scans can overlap; providers remain sequential after one activation. The per-type promise cache coalesces concurrent callers when a file-locator event has initialized caching; rejection clears only that same promise.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm successful results remain unchanged. On a cold canceled scan, the added guard rejects instead of admitting a partial positive/empty result; the existing catch evicts that rejected promise. The next request performs a fresh scan and can then become the warm cached result. No negative cache or retry loop is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed guard, surrounding Promise.all, cache assignment, identity-checked eviction, provider loop, and filesystem cancellation behavior were directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Filesystem and activation duration vary with workspace layout and extensions, but the added work itself is one token-state read and one exception only when the initiating scan was canceled.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff adds no expensive boundary or fan-out and prevents a canceled partial result from entering the cache. Re-execution occurs only after cancellation and a subsequent request, preserving intentional cancellation semantics.

Scenarios.Scenario: Warm or concurrent prompt discovery consumers, including all-type commands and customization migration
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A warm per-type call returns the cached promise before computeListPromptFiles, so it never reaches the new check. Cold calls for different types can run concurrently in all-type consumers; same-type callers share the existing promise when caching is active.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Discover local/user files for each cold prompt type requested by the consumer.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most two top-level standalone discovery branches per cold type; all-type consumers may request five distinct types concurrently, exactly as before. Warm per-type calls add no scans.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same per-type branch count and cross-type concurrency existed before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold consumers await discovery; warm consumers await or receive the cached promise. The token check does not affect uncanceled completion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Activate and query prompt-file providers for agent, instructions, prompt, and skill types; hooks have no provider activation event.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One activation event per cold supported type and sequential calls to providers registered for that type; warm results avoid these calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical provider cardinality, ordering, and cache coalescing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold discovery waits for activation/providers. The diff neither adds nor reorders these operations.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of distinct prompt types requested concurrently, configured locations, and providers. Same-type concurrency is coalesced by the existing cache; cross-type work remains independent.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All-type consumers use Promise.all across up to five types. Within each type, source branches overlap and providers serialize. The diff does not create an aggregate concurrency burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm cache hits return before the new line. Successful cold cache population is unchanged. If the token owning a shared cold computation is canceled, all sharers already observe that shared computation's outcome; the new behavior rejects and evicts rather than preserving a partial result, after which a later call may retry once.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: callers using Promise.all, the early cache return, per-type cache key, and changed post-computation guard were inspected directly.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The frequency of concurrent canceled and uncanceled consumers is unknown, but no automatic retry or newly introduced boundary exists.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The change does not alter warm-path work, normal cold-path cardinality, or concurrency; only canceled incomplete computations are denied cache admission.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over both changed files and the surrounding cache, provider, filesystem, built-in, and caller paths. The added post-computation cancellation check is constant-time and routes canceled partial discovery through the existing identity-checked cache eviction. It introduces no boundary work, retention, fan-out, or hot-path repetition. No performance findings and no qualifying performance regression fix were identified.
